stem: Which statement best describes digital transformation?
options: Replacing every on-premises server with a newer model that has more memory and storage
Moving the IT department into a separate company that sells its old hardware to other businesses
Using cloud technology to change how the organization operates and delivers value to customers
Scanning paper records into PDF files so that staff can find documents more quickly
explanation: Digital transformation is a change in how the business works and creates value, enabled by technology such as the cloud, data and AI. Digitizing documents or buying faster servers changes tools but not the business model or ways of working.

stem: How does a data lake differ from a data warehouse?
options: A lake is used for daily transactions; a warehouse is used to run the checkout system
A lake is kept on premises, while a warehouse is hosted on a public cloud
A lake stores raw data of any type; a warehouse stores structured data organized for analysis
A lake stores only structured tables; a warehouse stores only images and video files
explanation: A data lake holds large volumes of raw structured, semi-structured and unstructured data in its native format. A data warehouse holds cleaned, structured data modeled for analytics and reporting. Transaction processing is the job of operational databases.

stem: How is machine learning related to artificial intelligence?
options: ML and AI are unrelated fields: one is about statistics and the other is about robots only
ML is a subset of AI in which systems learn patterns from data instead of following fixed rules
ML is a broader field than AI, and AI is one technique inside ML
ML is a type of database, while AI is the reporting tool that reads from that database
explanation: Artificial intelligence is the broad field of making machines perform tasks that normally need human intelligence. Machine learning is a subset that learns from data. Generative AI is a further subset that creates new content.

stem: Attackers flood a company's website with traffic from thousands of machines until real customers cannot reach it. What attack is this?
options: Distributed denial of service (DDoS)
Phishing campaign
Ransomware encryption
Cryptomining malware
explanation: A DDoS attack overwhelms a service with traffic from many sources to make it unavailable. Google Cloud Armor and Google's global network help absorb and filter such attacks.

stem: A company moves its VMs to Compute Engine with no changes to the applications, to exit its data center quickly. Which migration approach is this?
options: Retire the application
Rehost (lift and shift)
Refactor the application
Reimagine the application
explanation: Rehosting moves workloads as they are, which is the fastest path but brings few cloud-native benefits. Refactoring changes the code; reimagining rebuilds the solution; retiring switches it off.

stem: How does moving from on-premises servers to the cloud change how a company spends on IT?
options: It shifts spending from up-front capital purchases to ongoing operating costs
It removes all IT costs, since cloud providers do not charge for computing
It requires the company to prepay for ten years of capacity on day one
It shifts spending from monthly operating costs to large up-front capital purchases
explanation: On premises, companies buy hardware up front (capital expenditure). In the cloud, they pay for what they use as an operating expense, which preserves cash and matches cost to demand.

stem: A retailer wants software that can take a customer's goal, plan the steps, use tools such as the order system, and complete the task with limited human direction. What is this called?
options: Agentic AI
Data warehousing
Business intelligence
Rule-based automation
explanation: Agentic AI systems pursue a goal on a user's behalf: they reason about the steps, call tools and systems, and act, with people setting guardrails. Rule-based automation only follows fixed instructions written in advance.

stem: A store collects purchase history from its own loyalty program. What type of data is this?
options: Synthetic data
Third-party data
Second-party data
First-party data
explanation: First-party data is collected directly by the organization from its own customers and channels. Second-party data is another organization's first-party data shared with you; third-party data is aggregated by outside providers.

stem: Which task is an example of generative AI?
options: Sorting customer records alphabetically by family name in a database
Showing a bar chart of yesterday's web traffic on a static dashboard
Drafting a first version of a product description from a short prompt
Adding up last month's sales by region in a fixed spreadsheet formula
explanation: Generative AI creates new content, such as text, images, code or audio, in response to a prompt. Totals, sorting and fixed charts are standard computing or business intelligence.

stem: Which statement about security in the cloud compared with on premises is correct?
options: Security works the same as on premises, with the customer running every layer itself
The customer becomes responsible for the physical security of the provider's data centers
The provider secures the underlying infrastructure, while the customer still secures its data and access
The provider takes over every security task, so the customer has none left
explanation: Cloud security is shared: Google secures the infrastructure it runs, and customers remain responsible for what they put in the cloud, such as identities, permissions, data and configuration. The split depends on the service model.

stem: During migration, a team moves its app to a VM but swaps its self-managed database for Cloud SQL. Which approach is this?
options: Replatform (move and improve)
Rehost (lift and shift) as is
Retain the app on premises
Retire the app completely
explanation: Replatforming makes a few targeted changes, such as adopting a managed database, to gain cloud benefits without rewriting the application.

stem: A startup does not know whether its app will have 100 or 100,000 users next month. Which cloud benefit matters most to it?
options: Data residency: data stays inside a single country
Open source: the code can be read by anyone at all
Scalability: capacity grows and shrinks with demand
Private cloud: the hardware is used by one tenant only
explanation: Scalability lets the startup add resources when users arrive and release them when demand falls, paying only for what it uses. The other options are real cloud features but do not address unpredictable demand.

stem: Which of these is an example of unstructured data?
options: Product prices in a relational table
Bank balances stored in a SQL database
Recorded customer service calls
A table of orders with fixed columns
explanation: Unstructured data has no predefined schema: audio, video, images and free text. Tables with fixed columns are structured. JSON with flexible fields is semi-structured.

stem: A bank's fraud rules have grown into thousands of hand-written conditions that miss new fraud patterns. Why is ML a good fit?
options: ML is the only way to store transactions safely, so the database can be removed
ML can learn complex patterns from past transactions and adapt as new data arrives
ML guarantees that every prediction will be correct for each transaction
ML needs no data at all, so the bank can stop collecting its transaction history
explanation: ML is well suited to replacing or simplifying complex rule-based systems: it learns patterns from historical data and can be retrained as patterns change. It needs good data and still makes some errors.

stem: A contractor needs to read reports in one project for a month. Applying least privilege, what should the administrator grant?
options: Editor access on every project, since the contractor is trusted
A read-only role on that one project, removed when the work ends
The Owner role on the whole organization, so nothing is ever blocked
The administrator's own password, shared for the length of the work
explanation: Least privilege grants only the access needed for the task, on the narrowest resource, for only as long as needed. Broad roles and shared credentials increase the damage if an account is misused.

stem: What happens in the discovery and assessment phase of a cloud migration?
options: Rewriting every application into microservices before planning
Switching off the old data center on the same day the project begins
Inventorying workloads and their dependencies to decide what to move and how
Signing up every employee for Google Workspace accounts in one batch
explanation: Discovery and assessment catalogs servers, applications and dependencies and evaluates each workload, so the team can choose an approach (retire, retain, rehost, replatform, refactor, reimagine) and plan the order of moves.

stem: In what order does Google Cloud's resource hierarchy run, from top to bottom?
options: Resources, projects, folders, organization
Folders, resources, organization, projects
Organization, folders, projects, resources
Projects, organization, resources, folders
explanation: The organization node sits at the top, folders group projects (for example by department), projects hold resources, and resources such as VMs and buckets sit at the bottom.

stem: A bank's leaders ask what happens if they keep everything on premises while competitors move to the cloud. Which risk is most likely?
options: Being legally barred from storing financial records in its own data center
Losing all customer data because on-premises servers cannot be backed up
Slower product releases that let more agile rivals win customers
Being forced to rewrite every application in a different programming language
explanation: The main risk of not adopting cloud is falling behind: slower innovation and time to market, higher fixed costs and weaker access to data and AI. On-premises systems can be backed up, and staying on premises does not force rewrites or break the law.

stem: A company wants to analyze petabytes of sales data with SQL without managing any servers or clusters. Which product fits?
options: Cloud SQL
Firestore
BigQuery
Bigtable
explanation: BigQuery is Google Cloud's serverless, highly scalable data warehouse for SQL analytics. Cloud SQL is for transactional relational workloads, Firestore for app documents and Bigtable for very high throughput NoSQL key lookups.

stem: A model predicting delivery times performs poorly because a third of the records have no delivery date. Which data quality dimension is the problem?
options: Uniqueness
Timeliness
Completeness
Consistency
explanation: Completeness measures whether required values are present. Uniqueness is about duplicates, timeliness about how current the data is and consistency about whether values agree across systems.

stem: Data is moving from a user's browser to a web application. Which encryption state protects it?
options: Encryption in transit
Data loss prevention (DLP)
Encryption in use
Encryption at rest
explanation: Encryption in transit, for example TLS, protects data as it travels across networks. Encryption at rest protects stored data, and encryption in use (Confidential Computing) protects data while it is being processed.

stem: What is a container?
options: A full virtual machine that includes its own separate guest operating system and kernel
A physical server cabinet that holds the hardware in a Google Cloud data center
A storage class in Cloud Storage for objects that are only accessed about once a year
A lightweight package of an application and its dependencies that runs the same anywhere
explanation: Containers bundle code with its libraries and settings and share the host operating system kernel, so they start fast and behave the same across environments. VMs include a full guest operating system.

stem: An organization worries about vendor lock-in. Why does Google Cloud's support for open source and open standards, such as Kubernetes, help?
options: Workloads built on them can move between environments with less rework
Open source software never needs security updates or any maintenance
Open standards make every Google Cloud product free of charge to use
Workloads built on them can run only in Google's data centers
explanation: Open source and open standards give portability: an application packaged for Kubernetes, for example, can run on premises, on Google Cloud or on another cloud. Open source still needs patching and is not a pricing model.

stem: A global payments company needs a relational database that is strongly consistent across continents and scales horizontally for both reads and writes. Which product fits?
options: Firestore
Cloud SQL
Cloud Storage
Spanner
explanation: Spanner is a fully managed relational database with strong consistency and horizontal scale across regions, suited to global transactional systems. Cloud SQL is managed MySQL, PostgreSQL or SQL Server for regional workloads.

stem: A lender uses an AI model to approve loans. Why does explainable AI matter here?
options: Explainability removes the need to test the model with any real data
Explainable AI lets the bank skip collecting training data
Explainable models always run faster and use less compute than others
Customers and regulators may need to know why an application was declined
explanation: Explainable AI helps people understand which factors drove a prediction. In high-impact decisions such as lending, that supports fairness checks, regulatory compliance and customer trust, which are part of responsible AI.

stem: A user signs in with a password and a code from a phone app, then can view but not delete files. Which step decides what the user may do?
options: Authorization
Encryption
Authentication
Auditing
explanation: Authentication proves who someone is, here with multi-factor authentication. Authorization decides what that identity can do, for example through IAM roles. Auditing records what was done.

stem: A team wants to be emailed when a project's spending reaches 50, 90 and 100 percent of its monthly plan. What should it set up?
options: A resource quota on the number of CPUs per region
A Cloud Storage lifecycle rule on the project's buckets
An IAM role that blocks all spending in the project
A Cloud Billing budget with threshold alert rules
explanation: Cloud Billing budgets send alerts when actual or forecast costs cross set thresholds. Alerts do not stop spending on their own; quotas and automated responses can enforce limits.

stem: A company needs full control over the operating system to run a legacy application that requires specific OS settings. Which product fits?
options: Looker
Compute Engine
Cloud Run functions
Firestore
explanation: Compute Engine provides virtual machines on Google's infrastructure, with full control of the OS, machine type and software. It is IaaS and a common landing spot for rehosted applications.

stem: A hospital keeps patient records in its own data center but runs its new appointment app on Google Cloud, and the two are connected. Which architecture is this?
options: Hybrid cloud
Public cloud only
Private cloud
Multicloud
explanation: Hybrid cloud combines on-premises (or private cloud) infrastructure with public cloud, working together. Multicloud means using more than one public cloud provider.

stem: A company must keep scanned contracts for ten years for legal reasons and expects to read them less than once a year. Which Cloud Storage class costs least for storage?
options: Archive
Coldline
Standard
Nearline
explanation: Archive has the lowest storage price and suits data accessed less than once a year, with a longer minimum storage duration and higher retrieval cost. Nearline suits roughly monthly access and Coldline roughly quarterly.

stem: A company needs to add image labeling to its app next week and has no ML team. The labeling does not need to be unique to the company. Which approach fits?
options: Train a custom model from scratch on TPUs
Hire a research team to design a brand new model
Build a rule-based system for every image
Use a pre-trained API such as the Vision API
explanation: Pre-trained APIs offer the fastest implementation and least effort, needing no ML expertise. Custom models take more time and skill and are worth it when the use case is a source of differentiation.

stem: A security team wants one place to find misconfigurations, vulnerabilities and threats across its Google Cloud resources, ranked by risk. Which product fits?
options: Security Command Center
Certificate Manager
Cloud Interconnect
Cloud Billing reports view
explanation: Security Command Center is Google Cloud's security and risk management platform. It discovers assets and finds misconfigurations, vulnerabilities and threats, and helps prioritize and fix them.

stem: A company runs dozens of containerized microservices and wants Google to manage the Kubernetes control plane. Which product fits?
options: Cloud Storage Nearline buckets
Compute Engine with one large VM
BigQuery ML with SQL models
Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE)
explanation: GKE is Google's managed Kubernetes service for deploying, scaling and managing containers. In Autopilot mode Google also manages the nodes.

stem: Which are the four golden signals for monitoring a user-facing system?
options: Uptime, budgets, roles and folders
Latency, traffic, errors and saturation
Cost, regions, zones and projects
Encryption, backups, audit logs and keys
explanation: Google's SRE practice measures latency (how long requests take), traffic (demand), errors (failed requests) and saturation (how full resources are).

stem: How are Google Cloud regions and zones related?
options: Regions and zones are two names for the same data center
A zone is a geographic area that contains several regions
A zone is a network edge location used only for caching
A region is a geographic area that contains several zones
explanation: A region is a specific geographic location, such as a city area, and is divided into zones, which are separate deployment areas. Running across several zones in a region protects against the failure of one zone.

stem: How does Looker help democratize access to data?
options: It removes the need to define any metrics, since each user is free to calculate revenue their own way
It replaces the data warehouse with a single shared spreadsheet that everyone edits at the same time
It gives business users governed, consistent metrics in dashboards and reports they can explore themselves
It copies every table to employees' laptops for private spreadsheets
explanation: Looker is Google Cloud's business intelligence platform. Its semantic model defines metrics once, so everyone sees the same governed numbers, and business users can explore data and build dashboards without writing SQL.

stem: What is Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform?
options: A spreadsheet add-on that only formats charts and has no access to AI models
A Google Cloud storage class for keeping old machine learning data at low cost
A hardware appliance that customers install to run email and file shares
Google Cloud's unified platform for building, deploying and managing AI models and agents
explanation: Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (the successor to Vertex AI) brings together access to Gemini and other models, tools to build and tune custom models and agents, and the runtime and governance to deploy and manage them.

stem: What powers Google Threat Intelligence?
options: Customer billing data, which shows where each company spends most of its money
Google's global visibility, Mandiant's incident response expertise and VirusTotal's crowdsourced detection
Passwords that customers send to Google each month for strength checks
A single antivirus product installed on each of a customer's laptops and phones
explanation: Google Threat Intelligence combines what Google sees across its products and network, Mandiant's frontline incident response knowledge and VirusTotal's crowdsourced malware data to give proactive insight into threats.

stem: A team wants to deploy a containerized web app that scales to zero when idle, with no servers or clusters to manage, paying only while it handles requests. Which product fits?
options: Cloud Run
Cloud VPN
Compute Engine
Bigtable
explanation: Cloud Run is a serverless platform that runs containers, scales automatically with traffic, including down to zero, and bills for the resources used while serving.

stem: Users in Sydney complain that a web app hosted far away feels slow to respond to each click, even though downloads are fast once they start. Which network measure describes the problem?
options: Latency
IP addressing
Bandwidth
Throughput cap
explanation: Latency is the delay for data to travel from one point to another, felt as slow responses. Bandwidth is how much data can move per second, which is why large downloads can still be fast. Serving users from a nearby region or edge location cuts latency.

stem: Thousands of delivery trucks send location events every few seconds. Which product ingests these events reliably so other systems can process them?
options: Archive storage
Pub/Sub
Looker
Cloud SQL
explanation: Pub/Sub is a scalable messaging and event ingestion service: producers publish messages and subscribers receive them asynchronously. It is a common entry point for streaming pipelines, often followed by Dataflow.

stem: An online store wants product pages available in 20 languages without training its own model. Which offering fits?
options: BigQuery ML
Cloud Translation API
Speech-to-Text API for audio
Vision API
explanation: The Cloud Translation API is a pre-trained model that translates text between many languages through a simple API call. Speech-to-Text converts audio to text, and the Vision API analyzes images.

stem: A company launches a generative AI chatbot and worries about prompt injection and the bot leaking sensitive data in its replies. Which offering screens prompts and responses?
options: BigQuery Omni
Cloud CDN
Cloud VPN
Model Armor
explanation: Model Armor inspects prompts and model responses to detect and block risks such as prompt injection, jailbreak attempts, harmful content and sensitive data leakage. It is one of Google Cloud's AI-focused security offerings.

stem: What is an application programming interface (API)?
options: A defined way for one piece of software to request data or services from another
A dashboard that shows business users the sales results for each region
A type of virtual machine that runs only on Google's own custom hardware
A storage class for files kept for legal reasons for ten years
explanation: An API is a contract that lets software systems communicate: one exposes operations and data, the other calls them, without needing to know how they are built inside.

stem: A team commits internally that 99.9 percent of requests each month will succeed, measured by the share of successful requests. Which term is the 99.9 percent target?
options: Service level objective (SLO)
Service level indicator (SLI)
Error reporting threshold
Service level agreement (SLA)
explanation: The SLI is the measurement (share of successful requests). The SLO is the target for it (99.9 percent). The SLA is a contract with customers, usually looser than the SLO, with consequences if it is missed.

stem: A team wants to deploy its code without managing operating systems or servers, but still write and own its application. Which service model fits?
options: Platform as a Service (PaaS)
Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
On-premises colocation hosting
Software as a Service (SaaS)
explanation: PaaS manages the runtime, operating system and infrastructure so developers focus on code. IaaS gives the most control but the team still manages the OS. SaaS is finished software, so there is no code of their own to deploy.

stem: Why is data governance important to a data-driven organization?
options: It sets who owns, may access and must protect each data set, so data is trusted and compliant
It is only needed by companies that keep their data on premises and never in the cloud
It deletes all historic data after each quarter so that storage costs stay as low as possible
It lets every employee copy any data set to any system without asking or leaving a record
explanation: Data governance is the set of policies, roles and processes that keep data accurate, secure, private and compliant: who owns it, who can use it and how. Good governance builds trust in the data that feeds analytics and AI.

stem: Data analysts who know SQL but not Python want to build a model that forecasts sales from data already in BigQuery. Which option fits?
options: Firestore
BigQuery ML
Cloud Translation API
Cloud Armor
explanation: BigQuery ML lets users create, train and run ML models with standard SQL inside BigQuery, so data does not have to move and analysts can use skills they already have.

stem: Which product protects internet-facing applications from DDoS attacks and common web attacks such as SQL injection?
options: Google Cloud Armor
Cloud Interconnect
Certificate Manager
Identity-Aware Proxy
explanation: Cloud Armor provides DDoS protection and a web application firewall at Google's network edge, in front of load-balanced applications.

stem: A company wants to query data stored in another cloud provider's storage using BigQuery, without moving the data. Which offering fits?
options: Compute Engine Spot VMs
BigQuery Omni
Cloud Run functions
Cloud Storage Autoclass
explanation: BigQuery Omni runs BigQuery analytics on data in other clouds, such as AWS and Azure, so it does not need to be copied. It is one of Google Cloud's multicloud offerings.

stem: What does the Domain Name System (DNS) do?
options: Encrypts traffic between a browser and a web server
Assigns each data center to a region and to a zone
Translates names like example.com into IP addresses
Stores copies of web pages close to the end users
explanation: DNS is the internet's directory: it resolves human-readable domain names to the numeric IP addresses computers use. Encryption is handled by TLS, and caching near users is the job of a CDN.

stem: A company wants to move its on-premises MySQL database to Google Cloud with as little change to the application as possible. Which target fits best?
options: Bigtable wide-column store
BigQuery data warehouse
Cloud Storage Archive class
Cloud SQL for MySQL
explanation: Cloud SQL offers managed MySQL, PostgreSQL and SQL Server, so a MySQL application can move with minimal change, for example with Database Migration Service. BigQuery and Bigtable would need the application redesigned.

stem: What are Tensor Processing Units (TPUs)?
options: Google-designed chips built to speed up machine learning
Storage classes for rarely accessed training data
Software licenses for SQL Server databases in the cloud
Network cables that link two Google Cloud regions
explanation: TPUs are custom accelerators Google designed for training and serving ML models. Along with GPUs they are part of the AI Hypercomputer's hardware layer.

stem: A European company must keep customer data stored inside the EU. How does Google Cloud help?
options: It lets the company choose the regions where its data is stored
It requires the company to keep the data on premises instead
It stores every customer's data in one global location only
It moves all data to the region with the lowest price each night
explanation: Data residency means controlling where data is stored. Customers choose regions for their resources, and Google Cloud offers controls for data sovereignty, such as limiting resources to approved locations.

stem: An operations team wants dashboards of CPU use and request latency, with alerts when they cross thresholds. Which product fits?
options: Cloud Interconnect
Cloud Translation
Cloud Profiler
Cloud Monitoring
explanation: Cloud Monitoring collects metrics, builds dashboards and sends alerts. Cloud Logging stores logs, Cloud Trace shows request latency across services and Cloud Profiler shows which code uses the most CPU and memory.

stem: Which two are business benefits of modern application development with microservices and managed services? (Choose two.)
options: Releases speed up because managed services handle routine operations
Teams can update one service without redeploying the whole app
Managed services require the team to patch all of the servers by hand
The whole app must stop running whenever any single service is updated
Every service must be written in the same language as all the others
explanation: Microservices let teams deploy, scale and fix parts of an application independently, and managed services remove operational chores, which speeds releases and improves resilience. Services can use different languages.

stem: A manufacturer is moving its analytics platform to the cloud. Which two outcomes are typical business benefits of that move? (Choose two.)
options: Removing the need for any staff to understand the data
Guaranteed zero downtime for every application, forever
Faster experiments, since new environments start in minutes
No need to plan any security or access controls at all
Paying for capacity as it is used, not buying for peak load
explanation: Agility (spinning up environments quickly) and cost-effectiveness (pay for use instead of buying for peak) are core cloud benefits. Cloud improves availability but cannot promise zero downtime, and the customer still owns access control and data skills.

stem: Which two are reasons real-time streaming analytics is valuable to a modern business? (Choose two.)
options: It means batch reports can never be used again by anyone
Stock levels and prices can react to demand within seconds
It guarantees that every incoming event is free of all errors
It removes any need to store data once the event has passed
Fraud can be flagged while a transaction is still happening
explanation: Streaming analytics processes data as it arrives, so the business can act in the moment: blocking fraud, personalizing offers, adjusting stock or prices. Batch analytics and storage still have their place, and data quality still has to be managed.

stem: Which two are examples of agentic AI reshaping how people work? (Choose two.)
options: A printed manual that lists every step of the company's return policy
A sales agent that researches a prospect and drafts a tailored proposal
A static report emailed to managers at the end of every single month
A support agent that looks up an order and processes the refund itself
A database index that makes customer lookups by ID run more quickly
explanation: AI agents act toward a goal: they reason, use tools and complete multi-step tasks, such as resolving a support case or preparing sales material, with people supervising. Reports, manuals and indexes do not act on their own.

stem: Which two statements describe a zero-trust security model? (Choose two.)
options: Once a user signs in, all systems trust them for the year
A strong perimeter firewall removes the need for any sign-in
Users on the office network are trusted automatically
Access depends on identity and context such as device health
Every access request is verified, even from inside the network
explanation: Zero trust assumes no implicit trust based on network location. Each request is checked against identity and context, such as user, device and location. Google's BeyondCorp approach and Identity-Aware Proxy apply it.

stem: Which is the best definition of cloud computing?
options: On-demand access to computing resources over a network, paid for as they are used
A single large computer that every customer shares at the same time on one OS
A company's own servers in a locked closet that only its staff can reach
Software that is installed from a disc and runs only on the user's own laptop
explanation: Cloud computing delivers compute, storage, databases and other services on demand over a network, usually the internet, with metered pay-as-you-go pricing. Self-managed servers are on-premises infrastructure.

stem: Which statement best explains why data is central to digital transformation?
options: It must be printed regularly to stay accurate
It only matters for companies that sell data
It reveals trends, informs decisions and fuels AI
It replaces the need for any company strategy at all
explanation: Data generates real-time insight, shows trends, guides strategic decisions and is the raw material for AI and ML. Its value comes from being collected, governed and activated, not from being printed or sold.

stem: Which best describes business intelligence (BI)?
options: Tools and practices for analyzing business data and showing it in reports and dashboards
A model that writes new marketing copy in response to a prompt from a business user
A chip designed by Google to train very large models much faster than general processors
A rule that every business decision must be made by an automated AI agent alone
explanation: Business intelligence turns business data into reports, dashboards and analysis that help people make decisions. It describes what happened; ML and generative AI predict or create.

stem: Malware encrypts a company's files and demands payment for the key. Which defense best limits the business impact?
options: Regular, protected backups that can be restored
Storing every file in one shared folder
A larger monitor for each employee's desk
A faster internet connection for the whole office
explanation: Ransomware is malware that encrypts data and demands payment. Isolated, regularly tested backups let an organization restore without paying; cyber resilience also includes detection and response.

stem: During assessment, a company finds an old reporting tool nobody has used in two years. What is the right migration decision for it?
options: Retire it
Rehost it
Reimagine it
Refactor it
explanation: Retiring switches off applications that are no longer needed, which reduces migration effort and cost. Retaining keeps an application where it is for now, for example because of a recent hardware purchase or a dependency.

stem: When comparing on-premises and cloud costs, why should a company look at total cost of ownership (TCO)?
options: It ignores hardware costs, since servers last forever once they are bought
It only counts the monthly bill from the cloud provider and nothing else
It is a security score that measures how well a company handles risk
It includes hidden costs such as power, cooling, space and staff time
explanation: TCO adds up every cost of running a system over its life: hardware, software licenses, facilities, power, cooling, maintenance and people. Comparing only server prices understates the on-premises cost.

stem: Which of these most often motivates an organization to pursue digital transformation?
options: A wish to keep the same processes for the next decade
Customers expecting faster, more personal digital service
A rule that every company must move to the cloud by law soon
A need to buy more on-premises hardware every year
explanation: Changing customer expectations and competitive pressure are the most common drivers. No general law requires cloud adoption, and keeping processes unchanged is the opposite of transformation.

stem: An airline shares its customer travel data with a hotel partner under an agreement. To the hotel, what type of data is this?
options: Public open data
Second-party data
First-party data
Third-party data
explanation: Second-party data is another organization's first-party data that it shares directly with you, usually through a partnership. Third-party data is bought from aggregators who did not collect it from their own customers.

stem: What is the difference between data analytics and machine learning?
options: There is no difference: both terms describe the exact same activity and tools
Analytics is a type of storage, while ML is a type of firewall that blocks attacks
Analytics examines data to find insights; ML builds models that learn from data to make predictions
Analytics needs no data at all, while ML works only on data that has first been printed out on paper
explanation: Data analytics studies data to answer questions and find patterns. ML uses data to train models that then make predictions or decisions on new data. They often work together.

stem: An employee receives an email that looks like it is from IT, asking them to sign in through a link to keep their account. What threat is this, and what protects best?
options: Phishing; security keys or other phishing-resistant two-step verification
DDoS; a larger web server that can handle more traffic at peak times
Physical damage; moving the office to a building with stronger walls
Cryptomining; turning off every VM at the end of each day
explanation: Phishing tricks people into giving credentials. Strong 2-step verification, especially phishing-resistant security keys, means a stolen password alone is not enough to take over the account.

stem: A company rewrites its monolithic order system into containerized microservices to use autoscaling and managed services. Which approach is this?
options: Replatform
Rehost
Refactor
Retire
explanation: Refactoring changes the application's code and architecture to become cloud-native. It costs more effort than rehosting or replatforming but gives the most cloud benefit short of reimagining the solution entirely.

stem: A company's cloud program is stalling even though the technology works. Which hurdle is the most common cause?
options: Cloud providers refusing to sign enterprise contracts
A culture and skills gap: teams resist new ways of working
The cloud being unable to run any kind of database
Cloud regions that cannot reach the company's branch offices
explanation: Transformation is as much about people and culture as technology. Skills gaps, siloed teams and fear of change are leading hurdles; training and executive sponsorship address them.

stem: Which is an example of semi-structured data?
options: JSON records whose fields vary from record to record
A photograph of a handwritten delivery note
A video recording of a store's checkout lane
A relational table with a fixed set of typed columns
explanation: Semi-structured data has tags or keys that give it some organization but no rigid schema; JSON and XML are typical. Video and images are unstructured; fixed-column tables are structured.

stem: A demand forecasting model is trained on sales data that is two years old, and its forecasts miss recent trends. Which data quality dimension is lacking?
options: Timeliness
Validity
Uniqueness
Completeness
explanation: Timeliness means data is current enough for its use. Old data can be complete and accurate yet still lead a model astray when conditions have changed.

stem: Which security principle ensures that data has not been changed without authorization?
options: Integrity
Compliance
Availability
Confidentiality
explanation: Integrity means data is accurate and unaltered except by authorized changes. Confidentiality keeps data from unauthorized people, and availability keeps systems usable when needed.

stem: In cloud migration, what is a workload?
options: The number of hours an IT employee works each week on projects
A contract that sets the price of Google Cloud for one year
An application or service and the resources it needs to run
A list of every file kept in an Archive storage class bucket
explanation: A workload is a specific application, service or capability together with the compute, storage and network resources it uses. Migrations are planned workload by workload.

stem: An administrator grants a group a role on a folder. What happens to the projects inside that folder?
options: The projects are deleted and recreated with new IDs
The projects move up to become part of the organization
The projects ignore it until each one is granted again
The projects inherit the access granted at the folder
explanation: IAM policies propagate down the resource hierarchy: access granted on an organization or folder applies to the projects and resources beneath it. That makes it efficient to manage access for whole departments.

stem: Which is one of Google Cloud's stated top differentiators?
options: Data centers located only in one country for simplicity
A promise never to support any open source software
A rule that customers use only one programming language
An AI-ready data platform with AI built into its products
explanation: Google Cloud highlights world-leading AI, an AI-ready data platform, the AI Hypercomputer, security, its global network and a commitment to openness and interoperability.

stem: In the data supply chain, what does data activation mean?
options: Putting insights to work, such as triggering offers or decisions in business systems
Creating the data for the first time, such as when a customer places an order online
Deleting old data that is no longer needed so that storage stays tidy
Moving raw data from one system to another without changing its format at all
explanation: The data supply chain runs from genesis (data is created) through collection, processing, storage and analysis to activation, where insight drives action, such as personalized recommendations or automated decisions.

stem: A data set contains birth dates in the future and ages of 300 years. Which data quality dimension do these records fail?
options: Validity
Timeliness
Uniqueness
Completeness
explanation: Validity checks whether values follow the rules and allowed ranges for the field. A future birth date or impossible age is invalid even if the field is filled in.

stem: How does Google Cloud treat customer data stored in its services?
options: It is encrypted at rest by default, with options for customers to manage keys
It is stored unencrypted unless the customer writes their own encryption code
It is encrypted only for customers who buy a premium support plan each year
It is encrypted only when it is sent over the internet and never once stored
explanation: Google Cloud encrypts customer data at rest by default. Customers who need more control can use customer-managed encryption keys in Cloud KMS, or supply their own keys.

stem: What does serverless computing mean for a development team?
options: The team must buy its own servers and install them in a colocation data center
The team must manually add a new virtual machine each time traffic goes up
There are no servers anywhere, so the code runs on no hardware
The provider manages the servers and scaling, and the team pays for what its code uses
explanation: Serverless platforms such as Cloud Run and Cloud Run functions still run on servers, but the provider provisions, scales and maintains them, so developers focus on code and pay per use.

stem: A media company runs its analytics on Google Cloud and its billing system on another public cloud provider. What is this arrangement called?
options: Hybrid on-premises
Multicloud
Single-tenant cloud
Private cloud
explanation: Using services from two or more public cloud providers is multicloud. Organizations choose it for best-of-breed services, resilience or to meet regulatory needs, and often manage it with open, portable tools.

stem: An IoT platform stores billions of sensor readings and needs single-digit millisecond reads and writes at very high throughput. Which database fits?
options: Looker
Spanner
Cloud SQL
Bigtable
explanation: Bigtable is a fully managed NoSQL wide-column database built for very large volumes and high read and write throughput with low latency, which suits time series and IoT data. Spanner is relational and chosen when you need global transactions.

stem: A retailer wants a model that recognizes its own product line on store shelves, which generic image APIs label poorly. Its team has little ML expertise. Which option fits best?
options: Use BigQuery ML to run a SQL query that counts products in the sales table
Train a custom model with AutoML on Agent Platform using its own labeled images
Write thousands of hand-coded rules that describe the pixels of each product
Use the Cloud Translation API to translate the product names into other languages
explanation: AutoML trains custom models on an organization's own labeled data with little ML expertise, which suits specialized needs that pre-trained APIs do not cover. It sits in Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (formerly Vertex AI).

stem: A healthcare company wants data to stay encrypted even while it is being processed in memory. Which offering fits?
options: Confidential Computing
Cloud Armor web firewall
Cloud VPN
Cloud CDN
explanation: Confidential Computing encrypts data in use, inside the processor's memory, using hardware-based trusted execution environments. Cloud VPN protects data in transit and Cloud Armor protects web apps.

stem: Which is a Google-recommended practice for cloud financial governance?
options: Let each engineer create resources with no labels at all so that the billing stays simple to read
Give all cost decisions to one engineer who does not talk with the finance team
Review cloud spending once a year, after the annual budget has already been spent
Name clear owners for cloud costs and have finance, tech and business teams review them together
explanation: Google recommends a cross-functional approach, often a central cloud cost team, with clear ownership of costs, visibility through labels and reports, and regular review. It is about people and process as well as tools.

stem: A team wants a small piece of code to run automatically each time a file is uploaded to a Cloud Storage bucket. Which product fits?
options: Spanner
Apigee
Cloud Run functions
Compute Engine VM fleet
explanation: Cloud Run functions (formerly Cloud Functions) runs single-purpose code in response to events, such as a file upload or a Pub/Sub message, with no servers to manage.

stem: When is a private cloud most likely the right choice?
options: When the company wants to avoid running and paying for any hardware of its own
When strict rules require dedicated infrastructure under the company's own control
When the company needs to scale to millions of new users within the next few minutes
When the company wants a provider to handle all patching of its hardware for it
explanation: A private cloud gives cloud-style self-service on infrastructure dedicated to one organization, which suits strict control or regulatory requirements. It gives up much of the elasticity and reduced hardware burden of public cloud.

stem: A mobile app needs a serverless document database that syncs data to phones in real time and works offline. Which product fits?
options: Cloud SQL
BigQuery
Bigtable
Firestore
explanation: Firestore is a serverless NoSQL document database with real-time listeners and offline support for mobile and web apps. BigQuery is for analytics, not app back ends.

stem: A call center wants written transcripts of its recorded calls to search them for common complaints. Which pre-trained API fits?
options: Cloud Translation API
BigQuery ML
Vision API
Speech-to-Text API
explanation: The Speech-to-Text API converts audio to text using pre-trained models. The transcripts can then be searched or analyzed, for example with Gemini, for themes and sentiment.

stem: An auditor asks who changed a firewall rule last Tuesday. Which security function answers this?
options: Encryption of the firewall rule at rest
Auditing through logs such as Cloud Audit Logs
Authentication with a password and a code on a phone
Authorization through an IAM role binding
explanation: Auditing records who did what, where and when. Cloud Audit Logs, viewed in Cloud Logging, keep records of administrative actions and data access for review.

stem: An online store's traffic triples during a sale. What do autoscaling and load balancing do together?
options: Add instances as demand rises and spread requests across the healthy ones
Move all traffic to a single larger server so that it is easier to manage
Block all new visitors until traffic returns to its usual daily level
Store copies of the store's database in an Archive storage class bucket
explanation: Autoscaling adds or removes instances to match demand, and load balancing distributes incoming requests across them and away from unhealthy ones, keeping the site responsive.

stem: How can an organization stop a test project from creating more than 50 virtual CPUs in a region?
options: Set a resource quota for that project
Move the project into a new folder
Create a monthly budget alert
Turn on Cloud Trace for the project
explanation: Quotas cap how much of a resource a project can use, which controls consumption and cost. Budgets alert on spending but do not cap it by themselves.

stem: What role do Google's edge locations (points of presence) play?
options: They bring traffic onto Google's network close to users, cutting latency
They store the master copy of every customer's database records
They are the only places where customers' VMs can run
They replace regions, so that zones are no longer required at all
explanation: Edge points of presence connect Google's private global network to internet providers near users and host content caches. Traffic then travels on Google's own backbone, which lowers latency. Workloads themselves run in regions and zones.

stem: A company runs a demanding PostgreSQL application and wants a fully managed, PostgreSQL-compatible database with higher performance for both transactions and analytical queries. Which product fits best?
options: Bigtable
Firestore
Archive storage
AlloyDB
explanation: AlloyDB is a fully managed, PostgreSQL-compatible database built for high performance on transactional workloads with fast analytical queries. Firestore and Bigtable are NoSQL and would mean rewriting the application.

stem: What makes Gemini models useful for many business tasks?
options: They only handle numbers and cannot read or write text
They are firewalls that inspect network traffic for known attacks
They are databases that store each customer's records for reporting
They are multimodal: they can work with text, images, audio, video and code
explanation: Gemini is Google's family of multimodal foundation models. Because it understands and generates across text, images, audio, video and code, one model family can serve many use cases, from summarizing documents to analyzing images.

stem: A security operations center wants to ingest large volumes of logs and telemetry, detect threats and automate responses on one platform. Which product fits?
options: Certificate Manager
Cloud Translation API
Google Security Operations
Cloud Storage Autoclass buckets
explanation: Google Security Operations (Google SecOps) is a unified security operations platform with SIEM and SOAR capabilities: it ingests telemetry at scale, applies threat intelligence, and speeds detection, investigation and response. Gemini in Google SecOps assists analysts.

stem: A research team runs batch jobs that can be stopped and restarted without harm. How can it cut Compute Engine costs?
options: Use Spot VMs, which are deeply discounted but can be reclaimed at short notice
Use the largest machine type, which always costs less per hour than small ones
Keep all of its VMs running all week even when no jobs are waiting to run
Move the batch jobs to the Archive storage class instead of running them
explanation: Spot VMs use spare Compute Engine capacity at a large discount, but Google can stop them when it needs the capacity back. That suits fault-tolerant batch work, not critical always-on services.

stem: A video studio uploads very large files every night, and the uploads take too long. Which network property should it increase?
options: IP version
Latency
Domain names
Bandwidth
explanation: Bandwidth is the maximum amount of data a connection can carry per second, so more bandwidth moves large files faster. Latency is the delay per round trip, which matters more for interactive apps.

stem: A team stores millions of objects in Cloud Storage and cannot predict which will be read often. What does Autoclass do for them?
options: Moves each object to a colder or warmer class automatically based on its access
Encrypts each object with a new key every time that it is read again
Deletes any object that has not been read by anyone within the last thirty days
Copies every object into BigQuery so that it can be queried with SQL
explanation: Autoclass automatically transitions objects between storage classes based on how often each one is accessed, which saves money when access patterns are unknown or change over time.

stem: How does AI Hypercomputer help an organization control the cost of AI workloads?
options: It offers flexible consumption models, such as committed, on-demand and Spot capacity
It makes every AI workload free once a company signs any kind of Google Cloud contract
It removes the need to choose hardware, since all AI runs on standard CPUs
It limits each customer to one small model so that bills never grow at all
explanation: AI Hypercomputer combines performance-optimized hardware (TPUs, GPUs), open software and flexible consumption models, such as committed use discounts, Spot capacity and the Dynamic Workload Scheduler, so organizations can match cost to need.

stem: A company wants employees to reach an internal web app from anywhere without a VPN, with access based on identity and device. Which product fits?
options: Bigtable
Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP)
Cloud Interconnect (Partner)
Cloud CDN
explanation: Identity-Aware Proxy checks each user's identity and context before letting them reach an application, an application of zero trust that replaces broad network access through a VPN.

stem: A company runs Kubernetes clusters on premises, on Google Cloud and on another cloud, and wants consistent management and policy across all of them. Which offering fits?
options: GKE Enterprise
BigQuery ML
Cloud Run functions
Cloud Storage
explanation: GKE Enterprise extends GKE with fleet management, consistent configuration and policy, and security across clusters running on Google Cloud, on premises and on other clouds.

stem: Which design choice most improves the resilience of a critical database?
options: Turning off monitoring so the database uses fewer resources
Replicating it across zones or regions and keeping tested backups
Running it on one large VM in a single zone to keep it simple
Storing its only copy on an employee's laptop for quick access
explanation: Resilient systems remove single points of failure through redundancy and replication, scale to demand and keep backups that are tested by restoring them.

stem: A company adopts Google Workspace for email and documents. Which statement about this service model is true?
options: It is IaaS: the company installs and patches the operating systems on servers
It is SaaS: the provider runs the whole application and the company just uses it
It is on-premises: the company buys the servers and places them in its offices
It is PaaS: the company writes and deploys the email app code itself
explanation: Google Workspace is Software as a Service: complete applications delivered over the internet, with the provider managing infrastructure, platform and software. The customer manages its users, data and settings.

stem: What is a key difference between relational and NoSQL databases?
options: Relational databases use tables with a fixed schema and SQL; NoSQL databases use flexible data models
Relational databases can only store images and video, while NoSQL databases can only store numbers
NoSQL databases must always run on premises; relational ones must always run in the cloud
Relational databases have no structure at all, while NoSQL databases always require a fixed schema
explanation: Relational databases organize data into related tables with a defined schema and are queried with SQL. NoSQL databases (document, key-value, wide-column) use flexible schemas suited to different access patterns and scale.

stem: Which is a key benefit of Google Cloud's AI offerings according to Google?
options: A single fixed model that cannot be tuned or grounded on company data
A rule that models train only on data stored outside Google Cloud
An all-in-one AI developer platform with access to first-party and other models
A guarantee that AI projects need no data preparation or governance work
explanation: Google points to its AI infrastructure, AI-ready data cloud, its own Gemini models (plus partner and open models), an all-in-one developer platform, and pre-built agents and applications.

stem: A trading firm moves large data sets between its own data center and Google Cloud every hour and wants a private physical link with high bandwidth, not encrypted tunnels over the internet. Which product fits?
options: Cloud VPN
Cloud Interconnect
Cloud Run
Cloud Armor security policies
explanation: Cloud Interconnect provides private physical connections, directly or through a partner, with high bandwidth. Cloud VPN creates encrypted tunnels over the public internet, which is quicker to set up but has lower throughput.

stem: A bank wants to expose account APIs to fintech partners securely, track how each partner uses them, and charge for usage. Which product fits?
options: Compute Engine VMs
Apigee API Management
Cloud Storage Nearline
Cloud Run functions
explanation: Apigee is Google Cloud's API management platform: it secures APIs, applies rate limits and access control, gives analytics on usage, offers a developer portal and supports monetization.

stem: A retailer opening stores in Europe and Asia wants its online shop to respond quickly for shoppers there, without leasing any facilities. Which cloud benefit does it rely on?
options: A private cloud that is dedicated to the retailer's own use
Global reach through the provider's regions around the world
Capital spending on new local servers in each of those cities
Open standards that run the same code on any laptop at home
explanation: Cloud providers operate regions on several continents, so a company can deploy close to new customers in minutes instead of building or leasing facilities, which would be capital spending.

stem: A company wants a single managed service to transform data in both streaming and batch pipelines without managing clusters. Which product fits?
options: Pub/Sub
Firestore
Looker
Dataflow
explanation: Dataflow is a fully managed service for unified stream and batch data processing, based on Apache Beam. Pub/Sub moves messages but does not transform them; Managed Service for Apache Spark suits teams that want Spark.

stem: When should an organization invest in building a custom AI model rather than using a pre-built solution?
options: When the use case gives a competitive edge and it has the data and skills to build it
When it needs a common capability such as translation working by next week
When it has no relevant data and no one on its staff who understands machine learning
When it wants the lowest possible development effort and the fastest launch date
explanation: Pre-built APIs and agents offer speed and low effort; custom models need more data, expertise and time but can deliver differentiation. The choice weighs implementation speed, effort, differentiation, skills and flexibility.

stem: Which is part of Google's secure-by-design infrastructure?
options: Letting every Google employee access any customer's data whenever they want
Purpose-built servers with custom security chips that verify the boot process
Running all customer workloads on hardware bought from an online auction
Relying only on a perimeter firewall around each of Google's office buildings
explanation: Google designs its own servers, networking and data centers and adds custom hardware such as the Titan security chip, which establishes a hardware root of trust so machines boot only verified software.

stem: A request passes through ten microservices and is sometimes slow. Which tool shows where the time is spent?
options: Cloud Profiler
Cloud Billing
Error Reporting
Cloud Trace
explanation: Cloud Trace follows requests across services and shows how long each step takes. Error Reporting groups application errors, and Cloud Profiler shows resource use inside the code.

stem: How can exposing public-facing APIs create new business opportunities? (Choose two.)
options: APIs mean the company's own apps no longer need to be maintained
Partners can build new products on the company's data and services
APIs stop competitors from ever building similar products of their own
APIs remove any need to secure the data that they expose to others
The company can charge for access, creating a new revenue stream
explanation: Public APIs turn a company's capabilities into a platform that partners and developers can build on, extending reach, and can be monetized directly. They still need security, which API management provides.

stem: Which two statements about IaaS are true? (Choose two.)
options: The customer manages the operating system and applications
It is a finished application used through a web browser only
The customer must buy and rack the physical servers itself
It offers the most control of the three main service models
The provider manages the customer's application code for it
explanation: With IaaS, such as Compute Engine, the provider runs the physical hardware and virtualization, while the customer manages the OS, middleware and apps. That gives the most control and the most management work. Finished applications are SaaS.

stem: Why do open, interoperable data platforms matter to an organization? (Choose two.)
options: They mean no access controls are needed on the data
They guarantee all data is accurate as soon as it lands
They help break down data silos between teams and systems
They prevent data from ever being shared with partners
They reduce the risk of being locked in to one vendor
explanation: Open formats and interoperable platforms let data flow between tools, teams and even clouds, which removes silos and keeps the organization free to change vendors. Governance and data quality work are still needed.

stem: Which two practices support responsible AI? (Choose two.)
options: Keeping humans accountable for high-impact automated decisions
Hiding how a model was trained from everyone who relies on it
Using any personal data available without checking consent
Testing models for unfair bias across different groups of people
Deploying models without monitoring once they have launched
explanation: Responsible AI includes fairness testing, transparency, privacy, safety and human accountability, plus monitoring after launch. Google publishes AI Principles that guide its own development.

stem: Which two help Google Cloud earn and keep customer trust? (Choose two.)
options: Hiding which locations store a customer's data from them
Selling customer data to advertisers to keep prices low
Transparency reports about requests for customer data
Letting staff access customer data without any records
Independent third-party audits and compliance certifications
explanation: Google Cloud publishes transparency reports, undergoes third-party audits for standards such as ISO 27001 and SOC 2, gives customers control over data location, and states that it does not use customer data for advertising.

stem: In cloud terms, what does infrastructure refer to?
options: The finished software that customers buy and then use through a web browser each day
The staff handbook that lists each employee's role, manager and allowed working hours
The physical and virtual resources, such as servers, storage and networks, that run applications
The business plan that describes how a company will earn revenue next year
explanation: Infrastructure is the foundation of compute, storage and networking that applications run on. In the cloud, it is delivered as a service and paid for as used.

stem: What is the main job of an operational (transactional) database?
options: Recording day-to-day transactions, such as orders and payments, as they happen
Holding raw files of every format before anyone has decided how to use them
Displaying dashboards and charts to managers who make business decisions
Storing years of history for complex analytical queries across the whole business
explanation: Operational databases support the applications that run the business, handling many small reads and writes quickly and reliably. Warehouses handle analysis, lakes hold raw data and BI tools show dashboards.

stem: What is generative AI?
options: A database that stores AI models and never runs them on any request from users
AI that only sorts existing records into folders by date and cannot create anything
AI that creates new content, such as text, images or code, from what it has learned
A security product that blocks attacks on websites at the edge of the network
explanation: Generative AI models learn patterns from large amounts of data and use them to produce new content in response to prompts. It is a subset of machine learning.

stem: A taxi company replaces its phone dispatch system with an entirely new app-based service built on cloud-native services and AI. Which migration approach is this?
options: Retain
Replatform
Reimagine
Rehost
explanation: Reimagining rethinks the business process itself and builds a new solution, rather than moving or rewriting the old one.

stem: A storage bucket holding customer records was accidentally set to allow public access. What type of security risk is this?
options: DDoS attack
Misconfiguration
Physical damage
Cryptomining
explanation: Misconfiguration, such as public buckets or overly broad permissions, is one of the most common causes of cloud data exposure. Tools such as Security Command Center detect it.

stem: Why does controlling cloud costs need people and process, not just tools?
options: Costs control themselves once a company has moved to the cloud fully
People and process matter only on premises and never in the public cloud
Tools show spending, but people must own costs and processes must act on them
Tools are not available in Google Cloud, so people must track every cost on paper
explanation: Billing reports and recommendations reveal waste, but someone must be accountable and regular processes, such as reviews and approval rules, must turn insight into savings.

stem: What is open source software?
options: Software that is free of every license term and obligation
Software whose source code is publicly available to use, study and change
Software that only runs on public cloud and never on premises servers
Software that a single vendor keeps secret and sells under a license
explanation: Open source code is published under licenses that let anyone use, study, modify and share it, subject to the license terms. Kubernetes and TensorFlow both began at Google and were released as open source.

stem: Which is an example of structured data?
options: A folder of photos taken at the company's annual summer staff picnic
Free-text reviews that customers post on a product page
Recordings of the support calls from the past six months
A spreadsheet of employees with name, ID and start date columns
explanation: Structured data fits a defined schema of rows and columns, so it is easy to search and analyze with SQL. Photos, audio and free text are unstructured.

stem: A logistics company deploys an AI agent that watches for delayed shipments, reroutes them and notifies customers. What makes this agentic rather than a simple chatbot?
options: It stores shipment records in a relational database for later analysis
It only answers questions when a person types in a message to it each time
It displays a fixed dashboard of shipments that someone must read and act on
It acts on its own toward a goal, using tools and systems to complete tasks
explanation: An agent goes beyond answering: it plans and takes actions across systems to reach a goal, within guardrails set by people.

stem: A company keeps one application on premises because it bought new hardware for it last year and will revisit the decision in three years. Which approach is this?
options: Refactor
Rehost
Retain
Retire
explanation: Retain means leaving a workload where it is for now, for reasons such as recent investment, licensing or dependencies, and revisiting it later.

stem: A company sees a sudden bill spike from many new VMs running at full CPU that nobody on the team created. What is the likely cause?
options: Cryptomining by an attacker using stolen credentials
Physical damage to a disk in a Google data center
A phishing email sent to an employee last year
A DDoS attack against the company's website
explanation: Attackers who steal cloud credentials often create resources to mine cryptocurrency, leaving the victim with the bill. Strong authentication, least privilege and threat detection reduce the risk.

stem: A finance team wants to see cloud costs broken down by department and application. What helps most?
options: Creating one project for the whole company with no labels
Labeling resources and using Cloud Billing reports to group costs by label
Asking each team to estimate its spending from memory every month
Turning off billing exports so the console shows only a single total
explanation: Labels are key-value tags on resources that flow into billing data, so Cloud Billing reports and exports to BigQuery can break costs down by team, app or environment.

stem: How does an open standard differ from open source?
options: An open standard is a cloud region; open source is a zone inside that same region
They are the same thing, and both terms refer to software that has no license at all
An open standard is a published specification anyone can implement; open source is published code
An open standard is code that only one vendor may ever change; open source is a paid support plan
explanation: An open standard, such as an API or file format specification, is publicly documented so many vendors can build compatible products. Open source refers to code that is publicly available. Both reduce lock-in.

stem: A marketing team buys demographic data compiled by an outside company from many public and commercial sources. What type of data is this?
options: Internal data
Third-party data
Second-party data
First-party data
explanation: Third-party data is collected and aggregated by an organization with no direct relationship to the people it describes, then sold or licensed. It is less precise than first-party data and raises privacy questions.

stem: A training data set contains the same customer transaction recorded five times. Which data quality dimension is affected?
options: Uniqueness
Timeliness
Completeness
Validity
explanation: Uniqueness means each real-world entity or event appears once. Duplicates skew models and counts, so deduplication is part of data preparation.

stem: What is a virtual machine (VM)?
options: A software-defined computer with its own operating system, running on shared physical hardware
A physical laptop that an employee takes home each evening to work on cloud projects at night
A database table that stores the names and sizes of a company's servers
A container that shares the host's kernel and holds only one application
explanation: A VM emulates a full computer, including its own guest operating system, on top of a hypervisor that shares physical hardware among many VMs.

stem: A user types instructions into a chatbot designed to make the model ignore its rules and reveal internal data. What is this called?
options: Phishing, a type of fake email lure
Ransomware, a type of file encryption attack
DDoS, a type of traffic flood attack
Prompt injection, a type of LLM attack
explanation: Prompt injection manipulates a large language model with crafted input to bypass its instructions. Model Armor and careful design of what the model can access help defend against it.

stem: Why is the cloud often more cost-effective for workloads with large seasonal peaks?
options: Cloud resources have no cost at all outside of business hours
Seasonal workloads are always free on any public cloud platform
You pay for extra capacity only during the peak, not all year
The provider pays for the hardware the customer keeps in-house
explanation: On premises, a company must buy enough hardware for the peak and let it sit idle the rest of the year. In the cloud, capacity scales up for the peak and back down afterwards, so the company pays for what it actually uses.

stem: Which order matches the data supply chain?
options: Activation, analysis, storage, processing, collection, genesis
Genesis, collection, processing, storage, analysis, activation
Storage, genesis, analysis, collection, activation, processing
Collection, activation, genesis, storage, analysis, processing
explanation: Data is created (genesis), collected, processed, stored, analyzed and finally activated as action in the business.

stem: A customer's address is different in the billing system and the shipping system. Which data quality dimension is this?
options: Timeliness
Validity
Uniqueness
Consistency
explanation: Consistency means the same data agrees across systems and data sets. Accuracy asks whether a value matches the real world; when two systems disagree, at least one is inaccurate and they are inconsistent.

stem: What is Kubernetes?
options: A Google Cloud storage class for rarely accessed backup files
A firewall that protects websites from DDoS attacks
A pre-trained API that translates text between many languages
An open source system for deploying, scaling and managing containers
explanation: Kubernetes orchestrates containers: it schedules them, restarts failed ones and scales them. Google created it and released it as open source; GKE is Google's managed version.

stem: Which principle is about keeping data hidden from people who are not authorized to see it?
options: Availability
Confidentiality
Resilience
Integrity
explanation: Confidentiality limits access to authorized users, using controls such as IAM and encryption.

stem: A research team needs a batch of GPUs for a training job and wants to obtain them cost-effectively when capacity is available. Which Google Cloud capability fits?
options: Certificate Manager
Dynamic Workload Scheduler
Cloud Billing budget alerts
Identity-Aware Proxy
explanation: Dynamic Workload Scheduler helps obtain GPU and TPU capacity for AI and batch jobs, for example starting a job when all the requested accelerators are available, which improves access and cost efficiency.

stem: Which benefit of cloud technology is a company using when it combines sales, web and supply data in one platform to spot trends quickly?
options: Physical security controls
Reduced latency
Data-driven insights
Single tenancy
explanation: Cloud data platforms bring data from many sources together at scale, so teams can analyze it and act on trends faster, which the guide lists as data-driven insights.

stem: Which Google Cloud product is object storage for files such as images, backups and videos?
options: Cloud Storage
Bigtable
Cloud SQL for MySQL
Spanner
explanation: Cloud Storage stores unstructured objects of any size in buckets, with classes from Standard to Archive. Cloud SQL, Spanner and Bigtable are databases.

stem: Why is high-quality data essential for a successful AI model?
options: Data quality only affects reporting dashboards and has no effect on machine learning
Models learn from their data, so errors and gaps lead to poor or unfair predictions
High-quality data makes models run without any compute resources at all
Models clean their own data automatically, so quality is never a concern
explanation: A model can only be as good as the data it learns from. Incomplete, outdated, duplicated or biased data produces inaccurate or unfair results.

stem: What is a microservices architecture?
options: A storage approach that splits large files into small Cloud Storage objects
An app built as small, independent services that communicate through APIs
A data center made up of very small physical servers in a single rack
An app built as one large unit that must be deployed all at the same time
explanation: Microservices break an application into loosely coupled services, each owning one function. Teams can build, deploy and scale them independently, often in containers.

stem: Why should privileged access, such as administrator rights, be tightly controlled?
options: Admins cannot sign in with two-step verification at all
A compromised admin account can change or delete almost anything
Privileged access makes applications run more slowly
Admin accounts are free, so they should be given to all staff
explanation: Privileged accounts have broad power, so attackers target them. Limit who has them, require strong authentication and log their use.

stem: A team moves an overnight rendering job to Spot VMs to control its cloud consumption costs. What trade-off should it expect?
options: The VMs cost more per hour than standard VMs, in return for priority access to capacity
The VMs must be bought up front with a one-year commitment
Google can stop the VMs at short notice when it needs the capacity back
The job can use only one VM at a time in each region
explanation: Spot VMs run on spare Compute Engine capacity at a steep discount, but Google can preempt them with about 30 seconds' notice. Jobs that can restart, such as rendering or batch processing, fit; critical always-on services do not. Commitments are a separate discount, committed use discounts.

stem: A company's IT staff spend most of their time patching servers. After moving to managed cloud services, they spend that time building features for customers. Which benefit is this?
options: Data residency: staff now choose which country the servers are located in
Physical security: staff no longer need badges to reach the server room
Strategic focus: staff move from undifferentiated work to value-adding work
Capital expenditure: staff now buy more servers well ahead of each new project
explanation: Managed services take on routine operations such as patching and backups, freeing people to focus on work that differentiates the business.

stem: A company keeps monthly backups that it may need to restore about once a month. Which Cloud Storage class fits best?
options: Standard
Coldline
Archive
Nearline
explanation: Nearline is designed for data accessed about once a month or less, with a 30-day minimum storage duration and a retrieval charge. Coldline suits roughly quarterly access and Archive yearly; Standard suits frequently used data.

stem: Which pre-trained API detects objects, text and faces in photos?
options: Cloud Translation API
Natural Language API
Speech-to-Text API
Vision API
explanation: The Vision API analyzes images to detect labels, objects, printed and handwritten text, landmarks and faces. It needs no model training.

stem: What does a managed service mean for an organization's IT team?
options: The IT team must manage every layer, including the physical hardware
The service runs only on premises and never in a Google Cloud region
The provider handles operations such as patching, backups and scaling
The service is run by a third party outside Google Cloud
explanation: With managed services, such as Cloud SQL or GKE Autopilot, Google runs routine operations, so the team spends less time on maintenance and more on its applications.

stem: A company wants to find and mask credit card and national ID numbers in its stored data. Which offering fits?
options: Cloud Interconnect
Certificate Manager for TLS
Sensitive Data Protection
