Cloud Run functions
explanation: Sensitive Data Protection (which includes the Cloud Data Loss Prevention API) discovers, classifies and de-identifies sensitive data, such as by masking or tokenizing it.

stem: In Google Cloud, what is a project?
options: A single virtual machine with a fixed name that cannot be changed
A container for resources, with its own settings, permissions and billing link
A folder of employees and job titles in the company's HR system
A storage class for objects that are read about once a quarter
explanation: Every Google Cloud resource belongs to a project. Projects hold settings, enabled APIs, IAM permissions and the link to a billing account.

stem: What is Google Cloud's AI Hypercomputer?
options: An integrated system of AI-optimized hardware, open software and flexible consumption for AI workloads
A single physical machine that each customer rents by the month to run its spreadsheets and its email
A program that certifies people as AI engineers after they pass a written exam
A chatbot that answers billing questions for Google Cloud customers on the website
explanation: AI Hypercomputer is Google Cloud's supercomputing architecture for training and serving AI: TPUs and GPUs, storage and networking, open frameworks and software, and consumption models that help control cost.

stem: A website serves product images that are read thousands of times a day. Which Cloud Storage class fits?
options: Coldline
Nearline
Standard
Archive
explanation: Standard storage has no minimum storage duration and no retrieval fee, which suits hot data that is read often. The colder classes have lower storage prices but charge for each read.

stem: A team wants to prototype prompts, ground a model on company documents and build an agent in a visual, low-code environment. Which tool fits?
options: Agent Studio on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform
Security Command Center findings and alerts view
The Archive storage class in Cloud Storage buckets
Cloud Billing reports in the Google Cloud console
explanation: Agent Studio (formerly Vertex AI Studio) is the console environment for testing prompts, tuning and grounding models and building agents with little code.

stem: Why might a company choose containers over virtual machines for a new app?
options: Containers start faster, use fewer resources and move easily between environments
Containers can only run on premises, which avoids any cloud costs at all
Containers do not need any code, so developers no longer need to write any
Containers include their own full operating system, so they are always more secure
explanation: Containers share the host kernel, so they are lightweight, start in seconds and run consistently from a laptop to the cloud. VMs offer stronger isolation and full OS control when that is needed.

stem: What does Identity and Access Management (IAM) control in Google Cloud?
options: Which region stores the cheapest data backups
Who can take which actions on which resources
Which language a chatbot replies to users in
How fast traffic moves between two zones
explanation: IAM grants roles, which are collections of permissions, to principals such as users, groups and service accounts on specific resources, so admins control who can do what.

stem: Why is Google's private global network considered a differentiator?
options: It only connects Google offices, so customer traffic never uses it for anything
It lets customers skip encryption, since one company owns the network
Traffic can travel on Google's own fiber backbone, giving lower latency and more reliability
It removes the need for regions, as every service runs on the network cables
explanation: Google runs one of the largest private networks, with subsea and land fiber linking its regions and edge locations. Customer traffic that enters it near the user stays on that backbone, improving speed and reliability.

stem: What is SQL?
options: A Google Cloud storage class for rarely accessed data
A network protocol that encrypts traffic between services
A language for querying and managing data in relational databases
A type of NoSQL document database used for mobile apps
explanation: Structured Query Language is the standard language for reading and changing data in relational databases. BigQuery and Spanner also support SQL.

stem: A company's chatbot gives confident but wrong answers about its own return policy. What would most improve accuracy?
options: Asking the model to answer faster with shorter replies to every user
Grounding the model's answers in the company's own policy documents
Removing all company data so that the model relies on general knowledge
Moving the chatbot's logs to a colder Cloud Storage class to save money
explanation: Grounding connects a generative model to trusted sources, such as company documents or search, so responses are based on current, specific facts. This reduces made-up answers, often called hallucinations.

stem: A team has a containerized API with spiky traffic and wants no infrastructure to manage. Another team runs a large set of microservices needing fine control over Kubernetes. Which products fit, in that order?
options: Compute Engine, then Firestore
Cloud Run functions, then Looker
Cloud Run, then GKE
GKE, then Cloud Run
explanation: Cloud Run suits individual containerized services with no cluster to manage. GKE suits teams that want Kubernetes features and control across many services.

stem: What does a VPC firewall rule do?
options: Translates text into many languages before it reaches the app
Encrypts data while it is processed in a VM's memory
Sends a budget alert when spending passes a set threshold
Allows or denies network traffic to and from resources based on set conditions
explanation: VPC firewall rules control which connections are allowed to reach or leave VMs, based on criteria such as IP ranges, ports and protocols.

stem: What do reliability and high availability mean in cloud operations?
options: They mean the same thing, and both describe how quickly a bill is paid each month
Reliability is consistently doing what users expect; high availability is staying up with minimal downtime
Reliability means never changing a system once it is live; high availability means running in a single zone
Reliability is the price of a service; high availability is how many regions it is sold in
explanation: A reliable system performs its function correctly over time. A highly available system stays accessible, usually through redundancy across zones or regions. Operational excellence is running and improving systems well.

stem: What is an IP address?
options: A domain name such as shop.example.com
The street address of the data center where a server is located
A password used to sign in to a cloud provider's web console
A numeric label that identifies a device or service on a network
explanation: An IP address identifies a network interface so data can be routed to it. People usually use domain names, which DNS translates to IP addresses.

stem: A company wants to stop paying for commercial database licenses and move to an open source-compatible managed database in the cloud. Which migration approach is this?
options: Retaining the database on premises and making no change to it at all
Modernizing to a different engine, such as moving to PostgreSQL on AlloyDB or Cloud SQL
Retiring the database and deleting all of its data without moving any of it
Lifting and shifting the same licensed database onto a Compute Engine VM with no changes
explanation: Moving to a different, open source-compatible engine is a modernization (replatform or refactor) that can cut license costs. Lift and shift keeps the same engine and licensing. Database Migration Service supports such moves.

stem: An insurer receives 50,000 claims a day and wants each one triaged consistently in seconds. Which ML business value does this show?
options: Scaling decisions that would otherwise need many people
Replacing all claims staff with one fixed rule
Removing the need to store any claims data at all
Guaranteeing that no claim will ever be fraudulent again
explanation: ML can apply the same learned judgment to huge volumes quickly and consistently, scaling decisions that people could not make fast enough, while staff handle exceptions.

stem: A company must keep a PostgreSQL database in its own data center for regulatory reasons but wants the same database engine it uses on Google Cloud. Which offering fits?
options: Cloud Run
BigQuery ML models
Firestore
AlloyDB Omni
explanation: AlloyDB Omni is a downloadable edition of AlloyDB that runs anywhere, including on premises and on other clouds, which supports hybrid and multicloud strategies.

stem: A company manages hundreds of TLS certificates for its websites and keeps missing renewals. Which product helps?
options: Sensitive Data Protection
Certificate Manager
Cloud Interconnect
Security Command Center
explanation: Certificate Manager provisions, deploys and renews TLS certificates for Google Cloud load balancers, which reduces outages from expired certificates.

stem: What is the goal of observability in modern cloud operations?
options: Printing server logs each morning for the operations manager
Understanding a system's health from its metrics, logs and traces
Reading every line of code by hand before any change is ever deployed
Watching staff through cameras to see who is at their desks
explanation: Observability means collecting and using telemetry, such as metrics in Cloud Monitoring, logs in Cloud Logging and traces in Cloud Trace, to understand and troubleshoot systems.

stem: A company wants its app to keep running even if one data center fails. What should it do?
options: Turn off autoscaling during busy hours
Run copies of the app in more than one zone
Move the app to a single edge location
Run the app on one much larger virtual machine
explanation: Zones are isolated from each other's failures. Spreading copies of an application across zones, or regions for more protection, keeps it available when one location has a problem. A bigger single machine is still a single point of failure.

stem: What does a company gain by visualizing its BigQuery data in Looker?
options: Faster transactional writes for the company's online checkout system at peak times
A way to store unstructured video files at the lowest possible price
Up-to-date dashboards and reports on live warehouse data, built into workflows
A full copy of the warehouse on every laptop, refreshed by email each week
explanation: Looker queries BigQuery directly, so dashboards and reports reflect current data, and insights can be embedded in apps or trigger actions in workflows.

stem: A hotel chain has years of free-text guest reviews. How can ML create business value from them?
options: By deleting the reviews so that storage costs fall to zero right away
By moving every review into a relational table with no other change
By converting each review into a fixed rule for front desk staff
By finding themes and sentiment across thousands of reviews at once
explanation: ML and generative AI can analyze large volumes of unstructured text to surface recurring complaints, praise and sentiment trends that would take people months to read.

stem: Which is a business benefit of running VMs on Compute Engine instead of buying servers?
options: Keeping each server in the company's own office for easy access
Never needing to manage the operating system or install any software
Paying for capacity as it is used and resizing it as needs change
Owning the physical servers so they can be sold again in the future
explanation: Compute Engine turns server purchases into on-demand capacity that can be resized, created and deleted as needed, with discounts for committed or sustained use. The customer still manages the OS.

stem: Which layers does Google Cloud describe securing in the AI stack?
options: Only the user's laptop and the office network
Only the billing account and the payment card
Infrastructure, data, models, platform and agents
Only the physical buildings and their power supply
explanation: Google applies defense in depth across the AI stack: secure infrastructure, protected data, safeguarded models, a governed platform and controlled agents.

stem: Which business case fits a hybrid cloud architecture best?
options: Moving every system to a single public cloud region in one weekend
Buying all new servers for a company that has never used the cloud
Using two public cloud providers for different analytics tools at once
Keeping a legacy mainframe on premises while new apps run in the cloud
explanation: Hybrid cloud lets an organization keep some systems on premises, often for latency, regulatory or legacy reasons, while using public cloud for others, with the two connected.

stem: A company has many existing Apache Spark jobs on premises and wants to run them on Google Cloud with little rewriting. Which product fits?
options: Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL
Managed Service for Apache Spark
Firestore document database with offline sync
Cloud Storage Autoclass
explanation: Managed Service for Apache Spark (formerly Dataproc) runs Spark and related open source workloads as a managed service, as clusters or serverless, so existing jobs move with minimal change.

stem: Which set lists the core components of Google Cloud's AI Hypercomputer?
options: Cloud Storage classes, IAM roles and the organization resource hierarchy
Looker dashboards, BigQuery tables and Pub/Sub topics and subscriptions
Cloud Armor rules, Cloud VPN tunnels and the Certificate Manager certificates
Performance-optimized hardware, open software and flexible consumption models
explanation: AI Hypercomputer is an integrated system: TPUs, GPUs, storage and networking tuned for AI; open frameworks and software; and consumption options that balance performance and cost.

stem: What does a load balancer do?
options: Sets a monthly budget alert for each project in the billing account
Distributes incoming traffic across several instances so none is overwhelmed
Translates domain names into IP addresses for users' browsers
Encrypts data at rest on persistent disks with a customer-managed encryption key
explanation: Load balancers spread requests across healthy back ends, in one region or globally, improving performance and availability. DNS resolves names, and Cloud Billing manages budgets.

stem: A company wants to discover all of its AI models and agents, assess their risks and detect threats against them. Which offering fits?
options: Cloud Storage Nearline lifecycle rules and labels
BigQuery ML forecasting models
Cloud VPN high-availability tunnels
AI Protection in Security Command Center
explanation: AI Protection helps organizations inventory AI assets, secure them and manage threats to them, as part of Security Command Center. It works alongside Model Armor.

stem: Among the golden signals, what does saturation measure?
options: How long each request takes from start to finish for the end user
How full a resource is, such as memory or CPU nearing its limit
How many users visit the site in a given minute of the day
How many requests fail with an error out of all the requests
explanation: Saturation shows how close a system is to its capacity limits. Traffic is demand, latency is time per request and errors are the rate of failed requests.

stem: A company compares running a database on a VM it manages, using Cloud SQL, and buying a finished CRM product. In that order, which service models are these?
options: IaaS, SaaS, PaaS (managed service)
IaaS, PaaS (managed service), SaaS
PaaS (managed service), SaaS, IaaS
SaaS, IaaS, PaaS (managed service)
explanation: A self-managed database on a VM is IaaS. Cloud SQL is a managed service in which Google runs the database engine, patches and backups, which is PaaS-like. A finished CRM product is SaaS.

stem: Analysts find the same customer listed three times with different spellings. Which data governance practice addresses this?
options: Making more copies of the customer table so each team has its own version
Moving the customer table to the Archive storage class to save money
Data quality rules and stewardship that keep records unique and accurate
Allowing every user to edit customer records without any review
explanation: Governance assigns owners (stewards) and quality rules, such as deduplication and validation, so data stays unique and accurate. More copies create more silos and inconsistency.

stem: Which is a business implication of not practicing responsible AI?
options: Having to use pre-trained APIs instead of training custom models later
Being unable to store any data in a public cloud region in that country
Models that always run more slowly than responsible ones on the same hardware
Loss of customer trust and legal risk if a model treats people unfairly
explanation: Biased, opaque or unsafe AI can harm people, damage reputation and break laws. Responsible AI practices reduce those risks and help adoption.

stem: Why is Looker listed among Google Cloud's multicloud offerings?
options: It copies all data from other clouds into a single Archive bucket first
It can connect to and model data in databases hosted on several clouds
It runs virtual machines on other cloud providers' physical hardware
It can only read data that is stored in Google Cloud and nowhere else
explanation: Looker connects directly to many SQL databases and warehouses, wherever they run, and provides one governed semantic layer across them.

stem: What does cyber resilience mean for an organization?
options: Being able to keep operating and recover quickly when an attack succeeds
Buying insurance instead of having any security controls in place
Keeping all systems offline so that no attacker can reach them
Never being attacked at all because the organization uses a public cloud
explanation: Cyber resilience assumes some attacks will get through and focuses on limiting damage, continuing operations and recovering quickly, through backups, redundancy, detection and response.

stem: A service's SLO is 99.9 percent availability, and this month it has used up nearly all of its allowed downtime. In SRE practice, what should the team do?
options: Raise the SLA promised to customers to 100 percent right away
Release new features faster, since the SLO no longer applies this month
Slow risky releases and focus on reliability until the budget recovers
Turn off monitoring so the remaining downtime is not recorded
explanation: The gap between 100 percent and the SLO is the error budget. When it runs low, SRE teams slow risky changes and invest in reliability; when there is budget left, they can release faster.

stem: Why might an organization choose a multicloud strategy? (Choose two.)
options: To guarantee that every provider charges exactly the same price
To use the best service for each job from different providers
To avoid having to manage identity or access for any users
To make sure that no data is ever stored in any public cloud
To meet rules or resilience goals that call for more than one provider
explanation: Organizations adopt multicloud for best-of-breed services, regulatory or resilience reasons and to reduce dependence on one vendor. It adds management work, which open tools such as Kubernetes help with.

stem: Which two pairings of need and Google Cloud product are correct? (Choose two.)
options: Managed MySQL for an existing web app: Firestore
Real-time document sync for a mobile app: Bigtable
Cheapest storage for files read once a year: Standard
Serverless SQL analytics on huge data sets: BigQuery
Global, strongly consistent relational database: Spanner
explanation: BigQuery is the serverless data warehouse and Spanner the globally consistent relational database. Firestore, not Bigtable, syncs to mobile apps; Cloud SQL runs managed MySQL; Archive, not Standard, is cheapest for yearly access.

stem: Which two needs can a pre-trained Google Cloud API meet without training a model? (Choose two.)
options: Detecting defects unique to one factory's parts
Predicting this company's own machine failures
Translating help articles into Spanish and French
Ranking products by this store's unique margins
Turning recorded meetings into text transcripts
explanation: Speech-to-Text and Cloud Translation handle general tasks out of the box. Predictions about a company's own machines, margins or unusual defects need custom models trained on its own data, for example with AutoML or BigQuery ML.

stem: Which two pairings of migration approach and description are correct? (Choose two.)
options: Retain: rebuild the solution around a new business process
Replatform: make a few changes, such as a managed database
Rehost: move as is, with no code changes
Retire: rewrite the application into microservices
Refactor: switch the application off for good
explanation: Rehost is lift and shift and replatform is move and improve. Retire switches an application off, retain leaves it in place for now, refactor rewrites code and reimagine rebuilds the solution.

stem: Which two pairings of security operations term and meaning are correct? (Choose two.)
options: Threat intelligence: a list of the company's own passwords
Threat intelligence: knowledge about attackers and their methods
Threat response: the encryption of data while it is at rest
Security posture: the overall strength of an organization's defenses
Security posture: the monthly price paid for security tools
explanation: Threat intelligence is information about threat actors, tactics and indicators. Security posture is how well an organization's controls and configurations protect it. Threat response is the actions taken to contain and recover from an incident.

stem: Which two statements about DevOps and Site Reliability Engineering are true? (Choose two.)
options: DevOps keeps developers and operations in separate silos
SRE requires that systems never have any downtime at all
SLAs are internal goals that customers never get to see
SRE applies software engineering to operations problems
Both aim to release changes quickly while keeping services reliable
explanation: DevOps is a culture that brings development and operations together for faster, safer delivery. SRE, which began at Google, is one way to practice it, using SLIs, SLOs and error budgets. SLAs are customer-facing agreements.

stem: Why do many organizations find the cloud can improve their security posture?
options: Cloud providers take legal ownership of the customer's data and its protection
Data in the cloud cannot be accessed by anyone, even its owners
Customers no longer need to decide who has access to their data or applications
Large providers invest in security expertise and controls that few companies can match alone
explanation: Hyperscale providers bring security engineering, hardened infrastructure and default encryption at a scale most companies cannot build themselves. Customers still manage their own access, data and configuration.

stem: A team keeps disaster recovery copies it expects to read about once a quarter. Which Cloud Storage class balances storage price and retrieval cost best?
options: Coldline
Standard
Archive
Nearline
explanation: Coldline is designed for data accessed about once a quarter, with a 90-day minimum storage duration. Archive is cheaper to store but costlier to read and meant for yearly access; Nearline suits monthly access.

stem: In machine learning, what is training data?
options: The examples a model learns patterns from before it makes predictions
The hardware chip on which a model is installed in the factory
The final report a model prints out after every prediction it has made
The password that protects access to a model's API endpoint
explanation: A model learns from training data, often labeled examples, and is then evaluated on separate data to check how well it generalizes.

stem: A company's public APIs are being overloaded by one partner's buggy script. Which API management feature helps most?
options: Publishing every API key on the company's website
Rate limiting (quotas) per partner, enforced by Apigee
Turning off all logging so that the API runs faster
Moving the API to the Archive storage class right away
explanation: API management platforms such as Apigee can enforce quotas and rate limits per consumer, protecting back-end systems while keeping the API available to other partners.

stem: A government agency needs assurance about where its data is stored, who can access it and that it can operate under local rules. Which concept is this?
options: Serverless computing
Digital sovereignty
Autoscaling
Load balancing
explanation: Digital sovereignty covers control over data location, operations and access under local laws. Google Cloud offers sovereign cloud options and controls such as data residency and access transparency.
